selection_method.screening_detail: All 591 titles were inspected. All 591 complete source bodies were machine-screened for US names/aliases, institutions, policy/legislation/electoral terms, and worldwide/conditional predicates; source matches were classified by their target, not by presence of government vocabulary alone. Full bodies for boundary families, title/criteria discrepancies, named-person targets, FDA/EPA decisions, NASA/EIA measurements, and positive/negative acceptance examples were manually inspected. This is not a claim of sentence-by-sentence manual review of every repeated body.
selection_method.topic_rule: Hold numerical questions involving US politicians/parties/policy/legislation/political entities, including explicit compound and conditional predicates. Specific US federal regulatory decisions are held under the parent campaign disposition. Non-US politics and government-associated scientific/business/technical measurements are not blanket excluded.
selection_method.global_rule: Worldwide existential predicates with no identified US actor or US policy target remain source-eligible. A generic any-country/any-candidate quantifier alone is not treated as an explicit US target. NATO-wide policy and Article 5 collective-defense commitments receive the explicit dispositions recorded below.
selection_method.conditional_rule: An explicit held US political predicate remains held if it is an antecedent or one clause of a compound, even when the other target concerns business, science, or non-US politics.
selection_method.past_event_rule: A completed past US election falling within an old source window is not used to authorize a new numerical political answer.
selection_method.independence_limit: Source targets and quotations were independently inspected; campaign boundary decisions communicated by the parent are identified as decisions, not treated as independent evidence that the source contains additional words. The parent-supplied account of Musk’s political role was not independently researched in this source-only review.

boundary_dispositions.basis: Explicit conservative named-entity boundary supplied by parent; source finance/science/entertainment contexts acknowledged. Does not apply to unnamed-person corporate Tesla/SpaceX targets.
Parent disposition: NATO Article 5 invokes a collective-defense commitment involving US foreign/defense policy, even without a named US member action in the source.
NATO-wide nuclear-policy adoption/change encompasses US foreign/defense policy.
Full source only says any candidate winning a Grammy; it does not identify a political candidate or the US. Its whole tuple can still be excluded by a political companion.

Outcome is an EIA-verified US energy-production fraction; antecedent is a worldwide unspecified national candidate. No identified US political actor or US policy decision in that question. Companion EPA predicates remain held.
Representative reviewed worldwide predicates: no identified US actor/policy target in the source. All variants follow the complete eligible/held ID partition, not this representative list.

semantic_caveats.detail: The full bodies preserve P, Q and R, including date windows. R and the conjunction both mix singular a new trade agreement with plural agreements. That is shared ambiguity about one multilateral agreement versus multiple agreements, not a cross-field change.

limitations: This is a reviewed subset of the original 300 groups / 591 questions, not the full benchmark.
Whole-group filtering removes eligible companion questions as well as held targets.
Source texts are unchanged; documented semantic defects are excluded, not repaired. This is not a formal semantic proof of all retained groups.
Scope decisions use source text and stated boundary dispositions, not model response values. Prior v2 observations existed before this scope was frozen.
All settings share source membership and protocol. Refusals/abstentions are retained and may shrink the scored intersection.
Historical and current campaigns differ in elicitation dates, native clients and prompts.
Named Musk personal-outcome targets and NATO collective-policy commitments are explicit conservative scope boundaries, not all mentions of US companies or technical agencies.
